subject.title: [Bug]: Task and Memory Recall Is Often Too Weak to Trust Across Real Conversations

question: Should #48711 become the canonical default project/task memory reliability plan, or should the remaining work be split under narrower opt-in memory/session issues?
rationale: Current code has partial mechanisms, but deciding defaults, privacy boundaries, task-state semantics, and live-gate scope requires maintainer product direction before implementation.

options.title: Make this the canonical reliability plan
options.body: Keep #48711 open as the umbrella, define the default project/task memory contract, and split implementation into focused PRs with a live gate.

options.title: Route to opt-in memory features
options.body: Treat existing Active Memory, sessionMemory, memory-wiki, and #99611 as the intended path, then narrow this issue to docs and configuration guidance.

options.title: Split and close the umbrella later
options.body: Create canonical narrower issues for task-state semantics, cross-session recall, stale-memory precedence, and cache-key diagnostics, then close #48711 once those are accepted.

recommendation.title: Make this the canonical reliability plan
recommendation.body: Keep #48711 open as the umbrella, define the default project/task memory contract, and split implementation into focused PRs with a live gate.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent main history and the earlier sessionMemory source work make steipete the best available owner for deciding whether this becomes the canonical memory reliability plan.
